    event_id text, -- example: ['rec0Si5cQ4rJRVzd6', 'rec0akZnLLpGUloLH']
    event_name text, -- example: ['March Meeting', 'Officers meeting - January']
    event_date text, -- example: ['2020-03-10T12:00:00', '2020-01-14T09:30:00']
    type text, -- example: ['Meeting', 'Election']
    notes text, -- example: ['All active members can vote for new offi', "Attend Women's soccer game as a group."]
    location text, -- example: ['MU 215', 'Campus Soccer/Lacrosse stadium']
    status text, -- example: ['Open', 'Planning']
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)
);

CREATE TABLE major (
    major_id text, -- example: ['rec06DF6vZ1CyPKpc', 'rec09LedkREyskCNv']
    major_name text, -- example: ['Outdoor Product Design and Development', 'Agricultural Communication']
    department text, -- example: ['School of Applied Sciences, Technology a', 'Watershed Sciences Department']
    college text, -- example: ['College of Agriculture and Applied Scien', 'College of Natural Resources']
    PRIMARY KEY (major_id)
);

CREATE TABLE zip_code (
    zip_code integer, -- example: [501, 544]
    type text, -- example: ['Unique', 'Standard']
    city text, -- example: ['Holtsville', 'Adjuntas']
    county text, -- example: ['Suffolk County', 'Adjuntas Municipio']
    state text, -- example: ['New York', 'Puerto Rico']
    short_state text, -- example: ['NY', 'PR']
    PRIMARY KEY (zip_code)
);

CREATE TABLE attendance (
    link_to_event text, -- example: ['rec2N69DMcrqN9PJC', 'rec5XDvJLyxDsGZWc']
    link_to_member text, -- example: ['recD078PnS3x2doBe', 'recP6DJPyi5donvXL']
    PRIMARY KEY (link_to_event, link_to_member),
    CONSTRAINT fk_attendance_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_attendance_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)
);

CREATE TABLE budget (
    budget_id text, -- example: ['rec0QmEc3cSQFQ6V2', 'rec1bG6HSft7XIvTP']
    category text, -- example: ['Advertisement', 'Food']
    spent real, -- example: [67.81, 121.14]
    remaining real, -- example: [7.19, 28.86]
    amount integer, -- example: [75, 150]
    event_status text, -- example: ['Closed', 'Open']
    link_to_event text, -- example: ['recI43CzsZ0Q625ma', 'recggMW2eyCYceNcy']
    PRIMARY KEY (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)
);

CREATE TABLE expense (
    expense_id text, -- example: ['rec017x6R3hQqkLAo', 'rec1nIjoZKTYayqZ6']
    expense_description text, -- example: ['Post Cards, Posters', 'Water, Cookies']
    expense_date text, -- example: ['2019-08-20', '2019-10-08']
    cost real, -- example: [122.06, 20.2]
    approved text, -- example: ['true']

    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_budget FOREIGN KEY (link_to_budget) REFERENCES budget (budget_id)
);

CREATE TABLE income (
    income_id text, -- example: ['rec0s9ZrO15zhzUeE', 'rec7f5XMQZexgtQJo']
    date_received text, -- example: ['2019-10-17', '2019-09-04']
    amount integer, -- example: [50, 200]
    source text, -- example: ['Dues', 'Fundraising']
    notes text, -- example: ['Secured donations to help pay for speake', 'Annual funding from Student Government.']
    link_to_member text, -- example: ['reccW7q1KkhSKZsea', 'recTjHY5xXhvkCdVT']
    PRIMARY KEY (income_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_income_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

CREATE TABLE member (
    member_id text, -- example: ['rec1x5zBFIqoOuPW8', 'rec280Sk7o31iG0Tx']
    first_name text, -- example: ['Angela', 'Grant']
    last_name text, -- example: ['Sanders', 'Gilmour']
    email text, -- example: ['angela.sanders@lpu.edu', 'grant.gilmour@lpu.edu']
    `position` text, -- example: ['Member', 'Inactive']
    t_shirt_size text, -- example: ['Medium', 'X-Large']
    phone text, -- example: ['(651) 928-4507', '403-555-1310']
    zip integer, -- example: [55108, 29440]
    link_to_major text, -- example: ['recxK3MHQFbR9J5uO', 'rec7BxKpjJ7bNph3O']
    PRIMARY KEY (member_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_member_zip FOREIGN KEY (zip) REFERENCES zip_code (zip_code),
    CONSTRAINT fk_member_link_to_major FOREIGN KEY (link_to_major) REFERENCES major (major_id)

In Scotland Premier League, which away team won the most during the 2010 season?
SQL: SELECT teamInfo.team_long_name FROM League AS leagueData INNER JOIN Match AS matchData ON leagueData.id = matchData.league_id INNER JOIN Team AS teamInfo ON matchData.away_team_api_id = teamInfo.team_api_id WHERE leagueData.name = 'Scotland Premier League' AND matchData.season = '2009/2010' AND matchData.away_team_goal - matchData.home_team_goal > 0 GROUP BY matchData.away_team_api_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

evidence: league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));
full_question:
league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));
Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
SQL: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id

SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN t2.preferred_foot = 'left' THEN t1.id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(t1.id) percent FROM Player AS t1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id WHERE SUBSTR(t1.birthday, 1, 4) BETWEEN '1987' AND '1992'

List the name of leagues in which the average goals by the home team is higher than the away team in the 2009/2010 season.
SQL: SELECT t1.name FROM League AS t1 INNER JOIN Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2009/2010' GROUP BY t1.name HAVING (CAST(SUM(t2.home_team_goal) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id)) - (CAST(SUM(t2.away_team_goal) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id)) > 0

highest potential score for crossing refers to MAX(crossing); preferred to use their left foots while attacking refers to preferred_foot = 'left'
How many players had the highest potential score for crossing that preferred to use their left foots while attacking?

only champion's finished time is represented by 'HH:MM:SS.mmm'; finished the game refers to time is not null; before year 1975 refers to year < 1975;
What is the average time in seconds of champion for each year, before year 1975?
SQL: WITH time_in_seconds AS ( SELECT T2.year, T2.raceId, T1.positionOrder, CASE WHEN T1.positionOrder = 1 THEN (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 1, 1) AS REAL) * 3600) + (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 3, 2) AS REAL) * 60) + CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 6,2) AS REAL )   + CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 9) AS REAL)/1000 ELSE 0 END AS time_seconds FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId WHERE T1.time IS NOT NULL ), champion_time AS ( SELECT year, raceId, time_seconds FROM time_in_seconds WHERE positionOrder = 1 ) SELECT year, AVG(time_seconds) FROM champion_time WHERE year < 1975 GROUP BY year HAVING AVG(time_seconds) IS NOT NULL

full_question:
born before 1985 refers to year(dob)<1985; in 2000 to 2005 refers to year between 2000 and 2005; percentage = Divide(COUNT(driverId where year (dob) <1985 and laps >50),COUNT(DriverID where year between 2000 and 2005) *100;
From 2000 to 2005, what percentage of drivers who were born before 1985 and the lap numbers were over 50?
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(STRFTIME('%Y', T3.dob) < '1985' AND T1.laps > 50, 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 on T1.raceId = T2.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 on T1.driverId = T3.driverId WHERE T2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005

question: Among the posts with a score of over 5, what is the percentage of them being owned by an elder user?
evidence: score of over 5 refers to Score > 5; elder user refers to Age > 65; percentage = Divide (Count(Id where Age>65), Count(Id)) * 100
full_question:
score of over 5 refers to Score > 5; elder user refers to Age > 65; percentage = Divide (Count(Id where Age>65), Count(Id)) * 100
Among the posts with a score of over 5, what is the percentage of them being owned by an elder user?
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T2.Age > 65, 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.Id) FROM posts AS T1 INNER JOIN users AS T2 ON T1.OwnerUserId = T2.Id WHERE T1.Score > 5

question: What is the average of the up votes and the average user age for users creating more than 10 posts?
evidence: creating more than 10 post refers to Count (UserId) > 10; average of the up votes = Divide (Sum(UpVotes), Count (UserId)); average age = Divide (Sum(Age), Count(UserId))
full_question:
creating more than 10 post refers to Count (UserId) > 10; average of the up votes = Divide (Sum(UpVotes), Count (UserId)); average age = Divide (Sum(Age), Count(UserId))
What is the average of the up votes and the average user age for users creating more than 10 posts?
SQL: SELECT AVG(T1.UpVotes), AVG(T1.Age) FROM users AS T1 INNER JOIN ( SELECT OwnerUserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count FROM posts GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING post_count > 10) AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.OwnerUserId

question: Calculate the difference in view count from post posted by Mornington and view count from posts posted by Amos.

Calculate the difference in view count from post posted by Mornington and view count from posts posted by Amos.

question: What is the average monthly number of links created in 2010 for posts that have no more than 2 answers?

full_question:
calculation = DIVIDE(COUNT(Id where YEAR(CreationDate) = 2010 and AnswerCount < = 2), 12)
What is the average monthly number of links created in 2010 for posts that have no more than 2 answers?
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T1.Id) AS REAL) / 12 FROM postLinks AS T1 INNER JOIN posts AS T2 ON T1.PostId = T2.Id WHERE T2.AnswerCount <= 2 AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.CreationDate) = '2010'

question: Among all the posts posted by the most influential user, identify the percentage with a score above 50.
evidence: The higher reputation the user has the more influence; percentage = DIVIDE(COUNT(stats_posts.Id where Score > 50 and MAX(Reputation))), COUNT(stats_posts.Id where MAX(Reputation));
full_question:
The higher reputation the user has the more influence; percentage = DIVIDE(COUNT(stats_posts.Id where Score > 50 and MAX(Reputation))), COUNT(stats_posts.Id where MAX(Reputation));
Among all the posts posted by the most influential user, identify the percentage with a score above 50.
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Score > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.Id) FROM users T1 INNER JOIN posts T2 ON T1.Id = T2.OwnerUserId INNER JOIN ( SELECT MAX(Reputation) AS max_reputation FROM users ) T3 ON T1.Reputation = T3.max_reputation

question: Among the comments with scores between 5 to 10, what is the percentage of the users with 0 up votes?

full_question:
percentage = DIVIDE(COUNT(UserId where UpVotes = 0 and Score BETWEEN 5 and 10))*100, (COUNT(UserId where Score BETWEEN 5 and 10));
Among the comments with scores between 5 to 10, what is the percentage of the users with 0 up votes?
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T1.UpVotes = 0, 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100/ COUNT(T1.Id) AS per FROM users AS T1 INNER JOIN comments AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.UserId WHERE T2.Score BETWEEN 5 AND 10

evidence: Chinese Simplified' is the language; percentage = Divide(Sum(id where language = 'Chinese Simplified'), Count(id)) *100
full_question:
Chinese Simplified' is the language; percentage = Divide(Sum(id where language = 'Chinese Simplified'), Count(id)) *100
Calculate the percentage of the cards availabe in Chinese Simplified.
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.language = 'Chinese Simplified' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid

full_question:
Story Spotlight card refers to isStorySpotlight = 1; French is the language; Percentage = Divide(Count(id) where language = 'French' and isStorySpotlight = 1, Count(id) where isStorySpotlight = 1)*100
What is the percentage of cards whose language is French among the Story Spotlight cards?
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.language = 'French' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.isStorySpotlight = 1

Diffrence in enrollement = `Enrollment (K-12)` - `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`

full_question:
Difference between K-12 enrollment and 15-17 enrollment can be computed by `Enrollment (K-12)` - `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`
Consider the average difference between K-12 enrollment and 15-17 enrollment of schools that are locally funded, list the names and DOC type of schools which has a difference above this average.
SQL: SELECT T2.School, T2.DOC FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.FundingType = 'Locally funded' AND (T1.`Enrollment (K-12)` - T1.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) > (SELECT AVG(T3.`Enrollment (K-12)` - T3.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) FROM frpm AS T3 INNER JOIN schools AS T4 ON T3.CDSCode = T4.CDSCode WHERE T4.FundingType = 'Locally funded')

question: List the names of virtual schools that are among the top 5 in their respective counties based on average reading scores.
evidence: Exclusively virtual refers to Virtual = 'F'; respective counties means PARTITION BY County
full_question:
Exclusively virtual refers to Virtual = 'F'; respective counties means PARTITION BY County
List the names of virtual schools that are among the top 5 in their respective counties based on average reading scores.
SQL: SELECT School FROM (SELECT T2.School,T1.AvgScrRead, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY T2.County ORDER BY T1.AvgScrRead DESC) AS rnk FROM satscores AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.cds = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.Virtual = 'F' ) ranked_schools WHERE rnk <= 5

non-chartered schools refer to schools whose Charter = 0; K-12 means grades 1 through 12; percent of eligible free rate for K-12 = `Free Meal Count (K-12)` * 100 / `Enrollment (K-12)`
What is the total number of non-chartered schools in the county of Los Angeles with a percent (%) of eligible free meals for grades 1 through 12 that is less than 0.18%?

question: What is the Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) in the school administered by an administrator whose first name is Alusine. List the district code of the school.

full_question:
Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) = `Free Meal Count (K-12)` / `Enrollment (K-12)` * 100%
What is the Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) in the school administered by an administrator whose first name is Alusine. List the district code of the school.
SQL: SELECT T1.`Free Meal Count (K-12)` * 100 / T1.`Enrollment (K-12)`, T1.`District Code` FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.AdmFName1 = 'Alusine'

    frequency text, -- example: ['POPLATEK MESICNE', 'POPLATEK TYDNE']
    `date` date, -- example: ['1995-03-24', '1993-02-26']
    PRIMARY KEY (account_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_account_district_id FOREIGN KEY (district_id) REFERENCES district (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE card (
    card_id integer, -- credit card id, example: [1, 2]

    CONSTRAINT fk_card_disp_id FOREIGN KEY (disp_id) REFERENCES disp (disp_id)
);

CREATE TABLE client (
    client_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    gender text, -- example: ['M', 'F']
    birth_date date, -- example: ['1970-12-13', '1945-02-04']

    PRIMARY KEY (client_id),

question: For the client whose loan was approved first in 1993/7/5, what is the increase rate of his/her account balance from 1993/3/22 to 1998/12/27?
evidence: Increase rate of his/her account balance = [(balance of date A - balance of date B) / balance of Date B] * 100%
full_question:
Increase rate of his/her account balance = [(balance of date A - balance of date B) / balance of Date B] * 100%
For the client whose loan was approved first in 1993/7/5, what is the increase rate of his/her account balance from 1993/3/22 to 1998/12/27?
SQL: SELECT CAST((SUM(IIF(T3.date = '1998-12-27', T3.balance, 0)) - SUM(IIF(T3.date = '1993-03-22', T3.balance, 0))) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(IIF(T3.date = '1993-03-22', T3.balance, 0)) FROM loan AS T1 INNER JOIN account AS T2 ON T1.account_id = T2.account_id INNER JOIN trans AS T3 ON T3.account_id = T2.account_id WHERE T1.date = '1993-07-05'

question: What is the percentage of loan amount that has been fully paid with no issue.
evidence: Loan paid with no issue means contract finished, no problems; status = 'A' means contract finished, no problems; Percentage of accounts by condition = [(total(amount) & condition) / (total amount)] * 100%
full_question:
Loan paid with no issue means contract finished, no problems; status = 'A' means contract finished, no problems; Percentage of accounts by condition = [(total(amount) & condition) / (total amount)] * 100%
What is the percentage of loan amount that has been fully paid with no issue.
SQL: SELECT (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'A' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100) / SUM(amount) FROM loan

Which are the top ten withdrawals (non-credit card) by district names for the month of January 1996?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T1.A2 FROM district AS T1 INNER JOIN account AS T2 ON T1.district_id = T2.district_id INNER JOIN trans AS T3 ON T2.account_id = T3.account_id WHERE T3.type = 'VYDAJ' AND T3.date LIKE '1996-01%' ORDER BY A2 ASC LIMIT 10
schema:
CREATE TABLE account (
    account_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    district_id integer, -- location of branch, example: [18, 1]
    frequency text, -- example: ['POPLATEK MESICNE', 'POPLATEK TYDNE']
    `date` date, -- example: ['1995-03-24', '1993-02-26']
    PRIMARY KEY (account_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_account_district_id FOREIGN KEY (district_id) REFERENCES district (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE card (
    card_id integer, -- credit card id, example: [1, 2]
    disp_id integer, -- disposition id, example: [9, 19]
    type text, -- example: ['gold', 'classic']
    issued date, -- example: ['1998-10-16', '1998-03-13']
    PRIMARY KEY (card_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_card_disp_id FOREIGN KEY (disp_id) REFERENCES disp (disp_id)
);

CREATE TABLE client (
    client_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    gender text, -- example: ['F', 'M']
    birth_date date, -- example: ['1970-12-13', '1945-02-04']
    district_id integer, -- location of branch, example: [18, 1]
    PRIMARY KEY (client_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_client_district_id FOREIGN KEY (district_id) REFERENCES district (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE disp (
    disp_id integer, -- disposition id, example: [1, 2]
    client_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    account_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    type text, -- example: ['OWNER', 'DISPONENT']
    PRIMARY KEY (disp_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_disp_client_id FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES client (client_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_disp_account_id FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE district (
    district_id integer, -- location of branch, example: [1, 2]
    A2 text, -- district_name, example: ['Hl.m. Praha', 'Benesov']
    A3 text, -- region, example: ['Prague', 'central Bohemia']
    A4 text, -- number of inhabitants, example: ['1204953', '88884']
    A5 text, -- no. of municipalities with inhabitants < 499, example: ['0', '80']
    A6 text, -- no. of municipalities with inhabitants 500-1999, example: ['0', '26']
    A7 text, -- no. of municipalities with inhabitants 2000-9999, example: ['0', '6']
    A8 integer, -- no. of municipalities with inhabitants > 10000, example: [1, 2]
    A9 integer, -- example: [1, 5]
    A10 real, -- ratio of urban inhabitants, example: [100.0, 46.7]
    A11 integer, -- average salary, example: [12541, 8507]
    A12 real, -- unemployment rate 1995, example: [0.2, 1.6]
    A13 real, -- unemployment rate 1996, example: [0.43, 1.85]
    A14 integer, -- no. of entrepreneurs per 1000 inhabitants, example: [167, 132]
    A15 integer, -- no. of committed crimes 1995, example: [85677, 2159]
    A16 integer, -- no. of committed crimes 1996, example: [99107, 2674]
    PRIMARY KEY (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE loan (
    loan_id integer, -- example: [4959, 4961]
    account_id integer, -- example: [2, 19]
    `date` date, -- example: ['1994-01-05', '1996-04-29']
    amount integer, -- example: [80952, 30276]
    duration integer, -- example: [24, 12]
    payments real, -- monthly payments, example: [3373.0, 2523.0]
    status text, -- example: ['A', 'B']
    PRIMARY KEY (loan_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_loan_account_id FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE `order` (
    order_id integer, -- example: [29401, 29402]
    account_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    bank_to text, -- bank of the recipient, example: ['YZ', 'ST']
    account_to integer, -- account of the recipient, example: [87144583, 89597016]
    amount real, -- debited amount, example: [2452.0, 3372.7]
    k_symbol text, -- characterization of the payment, example: ['SIPO', 'UVER']
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_order_account_id FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE trans (
    trans_id integer, -- transaction id, example: [1, 5]
    account_id integer, -- example: [1, 2]
    `date` date, -- date of transaction, example: ['1995-03-24', '1995-04-13']
    type text, -- +/- transaction, example: ['VYDAJ', 'PRIJEM']
    operation text, -- mode of transaction, example: ['VKLAD', 'PREVOD Z UCTU']
    amount integer, -- amount of money, example: [1000, 3679]
    balance integer, -- balance after transaction, example: [1000, 4679]
    k_symbol text, -- characterization of the transaction, example: ['SIPO', 'SLUZBY']
    bank text, -- bank of the partner, example: ['AB', 'YZ']
    account integer, -- account of the partner, example: [41403269, 87144583]
    PRIMARY KEY (trans_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_trans_account_id FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES account (account_id)
);
